title: Modi says government absorbed Rs 43 a litre of diesel cost to shield farmers from oil shock
dek: Speaking at a farmers' conference in Delhi, the Prime Minister said crude rose from $70 to $122 a barrel during the West Asia conflict but diesel went up only Rs 7, at a cost of Rs 14,000 crore a month.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Thursday that the government had absorbed Rs 43 of a Rs 50-a-litre rise in the cost of diesel caused by the West Asia conflict, passing on only Rs 7 to consumers, and that it was bearing a loss of Rs 14,000 crore every month as a result.

Speaking at the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026 in Delhi, Mr Modi said the price of crude oil "surged from $70 to $122 per barrel in just a few weeks" when war broke out in West Asia. "The government increased the price of diesel by only 7 rupees per litre, choosing to shoulder the remaining burden of 43 rupees per litre itself," he said, according to reports. He did not say when the Rs 7 increase took effect.

"In many of our neighbouring countries, diesel prices rose by 40% to 50%, but that did not happen in India," he said.

## The oil shock

The conflict between the United States and Iran, which began in late February, has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the route for a large share of the Gulf's oil exports. Global oil prices remain more than 40% higher than before the war, according to reports. India imports most of the crude it refines, so higher prices widen the import bill and put pressure on the rupee, which closed at 94.03 to the dollar on Thursday.

## Why diesel matters to farmers

Diesel runs most of India's tractors, irrigation pump sets and harvesters, and moves farm produce by truck, so its price feeds directly into the cost of cultivation and into food prices. Mr Modi spoke on the day official data showed retail inflation rising to 6.09% in October, above the Reserve Bank of India's 6% upper limit for the first time since October 2024, driven mainly by food prices. A day earlier the Union Cabinet had raised the subsidy on phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for the rabi season by about 64%, to Rs 62,370 crore, citing higher global prices.

The figure of Rs 14,000 crore a month, if sustained for a year, would amount to about Rs 1.7 lakh crore. Mr Modi did not say how the burden is split between the government and the state-owned oil marketing companies.

## Other announcements

Mr Modi said livestock belonging to more than 8 crore farmers would be vaccinated free against foot-and-mouth disease, and that about 12 lakh solar pumps had been installed under the PM-KUSUM scheme. He urged engineers and start-ups to develop solar-powered farm equipment.

He also made a pointed remark about the opposition without naming anyone, saying some people "think that the nation's Constitution and democracy reside in their pocket", according to reports. Opposition parties had not publicly responded to the remarks by Friday morning. The Congress has in recent months attacked the government over fuel prices and the ethanol content of petrol.

## What happens next

Crude prices have eased from their peak, with Brent trading around $92 a barrel on Thursday, according to market reports. The government has not said whether it will cut diesel prices if crude falls further, or how long it will keep absorbing the gap.
